annotations.text:
WHY THIS EXISTS

20 November 2026: Photos on the TV shipped (design/tv-photos/, A with C), but the hub does not know which of its screens is a TV. The panel works it out on the screen itself (onTV in tv.ts: a screen for the hub, in Chromium on Linux, that nobody can touch) and keeps it to itself. So the page says "the TV" where the board said "the living room TV", and the row is on This house in a house with no TV at all.

Every direction writes it on the screen's own record at the hub, beside the room it already keeps (phones.py), so the page, People and the TV's code can all name it.
TODAY. Photos on the TV and This house on a phone, from development after #56. Flip between them.

A: THE TV SAYS SO ITSELF. A screen the panel works out is a TV tells the hub so once, when it joins and whenever it starts. Nobody is asked. The page names it by its room ("The living room TV shows these"), and a house with no TV has no Photos on the TV row. Flip to see that house.

FOR: Nothing new to answer. The guess is the one the panel already acts on (the remote, the rows, the resting photos), so the name can't disagree with what the screen does.

AGAINST: A guess is still a guess. A TV the panel doesn't recognize (a smart TV's own browser, a box with a touch screen) stays a wall screen with no way to say otherwise.

B: ASKED ONCE, ON THE SCREEN, WHEN IT JOINS. Before which room it is in, a new screen asks what it is, with the panel's guess already lit so OK confirms it. A TV rests on photos and is worked with the remote; a wall screen rests on the clock. This screen gets the same question as a row, to change it later. The page then names it as in A.

FOR: Right every time, including the TVs the guess misses, and it's said by whoever is standing in front of it. AGAINST: One more question in a join that is already two (the passcode, the room), for an answer that is nearly always the guess.

C: THE HOUSEHOLD CHOOSES WHICH SCREENS SHOW PHOTOS. The page becomes Photos, and lists the house's screens with a switch each. A TV starts on (found as in A); a wall screen starts off and shows the clock, but a household can turn its hallway into a frame too.

FOR: Answers the next question too ("can the kitchen screen show them?") and never needs the word TV to be right. AGAINST: A setting nobody asked for yet, and it reopens what a wall screen rests on, which design/rest/ settled.

CHOSEN WITH A (20 November): the household wants the hallway able to show photos too. A wall screen showing them is drawn on its own page, "A wall screen that shows photos at rest", because the wall's rest is design/rest/'s.

DECIDED 20 NOVEMBER 2026 -- A, WITH B AS A ROW ON THIS SCREEN, AND C'S CHOICE OF SCREENS

A screen the panel works out is a TV says so to the hub, and nobody is asked. This screen gets one row, What it is (A TV / On the wall), for the TV the guess got wrong; an answer there is kept by the hub and beats the guess from then on. The page is C's: Photos, with each of the house's screens and a switch, a TV on to start and a wall screen off. It names the TVs by their rooms. A house with no screens has no Photos row.

How a wall screen looks while it shows photos is the next page's question.

B'S QUESTION, ON THIS SCREEN. Under Room, What it is: the answer in words and the two choices, the guess lit. Choosing restarts the screen as the other kind, because a TV and a wall are worked differently from the first frame (the remote and its rows, or touch). Not asked when a screen joins.

NOT CHOSEN

B as a question when a screen joins: one more question for an answer that is nearly always the guess. Kept as a row on This screen instead.

A WALL SCREEN THAT SHOWS PHOTOS

With C, a household can switch a wall screen's photos on. The wall's rest was settled on 28 September (design/rest/, CornerF: the clock, the date, four facts and the weather in the corner), so how it looks over a photo is drawn here before it is built. Touch wakes it as today; there is no OK line.
TODAY. The wall at rest, from development: the sky, the clock, four facts, the weather in the corner.

WALL A: THE TV'S PHOTOS, AT THE WALL'S SIZE. The resting TV's photo face as built (TvRest), scaled to 1440 x 900: the photo fills the screen, when and whose along the top, the clock bottom left, three facts bottom right. FOR: one look for photos on every screen, and nothing new to build or keep. AGAINST: the wall's four facts become three small ones, and a hallway glance reads them less well than CornerF's.

WALL B: THE WALL'S OWN REST, OVER THE PHOTO. CornerF exactly, the clock, the date, the four facts and the weather in the corner, with the photo where the sky was and a soft wash behind the words. FOR: the wall still reads the same from across the hallway; only the picture behind changes. AGAINST: the words sit on the middle of the photo, so the photo is mostly the edges.

WALL C: THE PHOTO FRAMED, THE HOUSE ON A BAND. The photo fills the top four fifths untouched; a dark band along the foot holds the clock and the four facts, like a caption under a print. FOR: the photo is never covered, and nothing has to fight it for contrast. AGAINST: the clock is smaller than either A or B, and the band is a new shape for the wall.

DECIDED 20 NOVEMBER 2026 -- A

A wall screen with its photos switched on rests on the TV's photo face, at its own size: the photo, when and whose along the top, the clock bottom left, three facts bottom right, and no OK line, since a wall is touched. With its photos off, or no photos yet, it rests as CornerF does. Bedtime and the music face stay the TV's.

NOT CHOSEN

B put the wall's words over the middle of the photo; C made the clock smaller and gave the wall a new shape. A is one look for photos on every screen.
